Definition: from G5092; valuable; Timon, a Christian:--Timon.
BiblicalUsage: Timon is named once, and the naming is honour enough. When the whole multitude chose seven men to serve the tables, they chose Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas and Nicolas, and Luke lists him among the first deacons of the church.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the list is the point: the church's first servants are named one by one, and Timon stands in the company of Stephen and Philip, chosen because the work mattered and the men were trusted.
